name: loop-kit-dev
description: [DEV] Flow and turn-gate loop plugin that shapes work into flows and keeps one turn alive until explicit user stop.

interface.shortDescription: [DEV] Flow rules plus turn-gated continuity for multi-flow agent work.
interface.longDescription: [DEV] Provides a loop-oriented plugin with two coordinated surfaces. Flow classifies messages and actions into active flows, parent flows, finite sub-flow candidates, operational-preparation flows, and change-unit flows, then owns readiness, discovery, flow-local strategy, and handoff conditions. Turn-gate keeps one turn alive until the user explicitly ends it, requires work to move through flow contracts, reopens next-flow choices after reporting, records continuity, and chooses verification method as clean-context, normal, or not-required based on work risk. Self-drive is a separate overlay reference for prepared flow sequences.
defaultPrompt: Use flow to classify work into active flows, parent flows, finite sub-flow candidates, operational-preparation flows, and change-unit flows.
Let flow own readiness, discovery questions, flow-local execution strategy, and handoff conditions; do not make turn-gate redefine those strategy decisions.
Treat sub-flow candidate creation as planning output, not execution; activate a sub-flow only through turn-gate next-flow routing or a prepared self-drive sequence.
Keep this turn alive until I explicitly stop; after reporting, reopen next-flow with explicit choices unless closure is source-recorded.
Run each active flow through preparation, work, verification, and reporting, then let turn-gate handle next-flow reopening.
Treat flows as cohesive reviewable or commit-sized units, not analysis/work/verification phase slices and not only direct user-visible value.
Classify verification method as clean-context, normal, or not-required while keeping result status separate as pass, fail, blocked, or insufficient.
Use clean-context verifier by default for file changes, release surfaces, multi-file contracts, failed checks, user-requested verification, and approval-sensitive actions.
Use normal evidence checks only for lower-risk no-edit/read-only work, and use not-required only when there is no work output to verify; always record reason and residual uncertainty.
Never infer approval for destructive, external, commit, push, PR, publish, release, or version bump actions from readiness, self-drive, verification method, or prior context.
Use turn-gate as the turn-level gate for continuity, explicit stop handling, session records, and next-flow reopening; keep self-drive as a separate overlay for explicitly prepared flow sequences.
